chapter: Learning the drums and first job
title: Lessons with Louis Cottrell
summary: He took lessons from strict teacher Louis Cottrell, recommended by his father, but gave up reading; Cottrell played with Perez at the roof garden.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: 19. Yeah. Now, did you have a teacher?
Well, I started with Louis Contrell, Mr. Contrell, the old drummer.
Yeah. I never knew him, but I know his son, of course.
Yeah. My daddy recommended to him, you know.
And I took a few lessons with him and then, I don't know, I just stopped and I liked the jazz. I didn't care too much about reading. I'm sorry I didn't keep it up then.
Yeah. Well, a lot of good drummers never did bother with the reading anyway, of course.
But he was very interested, man. I should have kept...
Was he a pretty strict teacher? Yeah, he was pretty strict.
You couldn't put nothing in it. You couldn't put nothing over.
You know who he was playing with in those days or what band he was in?
He was playing with Manny Perez on the roof garden.
Up there where the city hall is now. Deeply Temple. Yeah, right there.
